clue.text: Earthshaking doctrine one penned in a trice

indicators.note: penned in says the doctrine and the one are enclosed inside the short moment

parts.note: a trice is a very short time, a sec
an ism is a doctrine or creed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A world-shaking creed is written down in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic describes tremors of the earth, so figuratively anything momentous or upheaving.

clue.text: Hardy shrub no good in Arab country

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for no good inside the name of the country

parts.note: Syria is an Arab country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A tough bush won't grow well in a Middle Eastern land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus of lilac, a robust flowering bush.

clue.text: Is all femininity suspect? Ever so slightly

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious or unsound, tells us to rework the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if all womanliness is dubious, but only a tiny bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the fifteen letters of IS ALL FEMININITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimally means by an immeasurably tiny amount, a minimal degree.

clue.text: Turned up snatch of tune, impromptu air

indicators.note: Turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
snatch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician plays a fragment of an improvised melody, turning it upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Turned up' reads the hidden run NEIM (in tuNE IMpromptu) from bottom to top, giving the answer. 'air' looks musical alongside 'tune' but means bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien and air both mean a person's manner or bearing, the impression they give.

clue.text: Adopt bilateral domestic policy?

parts.note: reads like a political programme agreed between two states, but means two people deciding to share a home as a couple

explanation.surface: A government announces a two-sided policy on home affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Living together as partners without marrying is a household arrangement agreed by both sides.

clue.text: Archdeacon is against having meat

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
taken as written
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A senior cleric declares himself opposed to eating meat.
explanation.walkthrough: An Anglican archdeacon carries the title 'the Venerable', shortened to VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food.

clue.text: Managed to go through Hindu text in gallery

indicators.note: to go through says one piece passes inside the other

parts.note: the Veda is an ancient body of Hindu scripture
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in reading a sacred Hindu work in an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open gallery or porch along the outside of a house.

clue.text: Relations finally abandoned secluded retreat

indicators.note: finally abandoned says the last letter of the word for relations is dropped

parts.note: nooky is slang for sexual relations

explanation.surface: Family members at last desert a quiet hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives, but it means sexual relations, the slang NOOKY, whose last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered, out-of-the-way corner where one can withdraw.

clue.text: Poker hand with which you'll see player open

parts.note: a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence
a forward is an attacking player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A card game: with a certain hand you get to see another player's cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward and open both describe frank, honest behaviour with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Necessary for Nebraska feud to be resolved on third of July

parts.note: NE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nebraska

indicators.note: a feud resolved is settled; here the letters are reworked into a new order
third of picks the third letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dispute in a US state must be settled on the third of July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be resolved' turns FEUD into EDFU; 'third of July' gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an old-fashioned word for required or essential.

clue.text: Divinity student new on track for more training

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject of divinity
a fresher is a new student in their first term
a course is a track, as in a racecourse

explanation.surface: A theology undergraduate just starting out is on a path to further study.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a FRESHER is a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a short programme updating someone's skills, i.e. extra instruction.

clue.text: Number in African state wanting bishop back

indicators.note: back says the remaining letters are read in reverse order
wanting means lacking, so the letter for bishop is taken away

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A figure in a West African country wants its bishop to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes B from BENIN, leaving ENIN, which 'back' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a cardinal figure, one more than eight.

clue.text: Wood from Spain, very thin

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
bony describes someone so thin their bones show

explanation.surface: Timber imported from Spain is extremely slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense black hardwood from tropical trees.

clue.text: Quarrel apt to turn loud

indicators.note: to turn says the word for apt is reversed

parts.note: fit means apt or suitable
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: An argument is liable to become noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt to turn' reads like 'likely to become', but 'apt' is FIT and 'to turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor squabble or spat.

clue.text: Dark brown figure, with head missing

indicators.note: with head missing says the first letter of the word for figure is dropped

parts.note: a number is a figure, such as 7

explanation.surface: A dark brown statue has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a statue, but it is NUMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment of deep brown colour.

clue.text: Cake is served with ice-cream

parts.note: is shortens to 's
a cone is an ice-cream in a wafer cornet

explanation.surface: A café serves a pastry alongside a frozen dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small baked bun or teacake, often eaten with jam and cream.

clue.text: Son going to give evidence about politician is shot

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes around the politician
going means departing, so the letter for son leaves

parts.note: to attest is to give evidence or bear witness
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A man's son will testify about an MP who has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son going' leaves ATTET for 'about' to wrap round. 'shot' means a try, not a gunshot, and 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot and an attempt both mean a try at something, as in 'have a go'.

clue.text: House officer first to have everyone round for drink

indicators.note: round says the word for everyone surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: first says officer is placed before house

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A house officer begins by inviting everyone round for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'house officer' is a junior hospital doctor, but here 'first' reorders the two abbreviations so officer comes before House.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is booze, the intoxicating ingredient in beer, wine and spirits.

clue.text: Mother Superior steals scene, replacing a bishop -it matters

indicators.note: replacing says one letter in the nun's title is swapped for another piece

parts.note: an abbess is the head of a convent, a Mother Superior
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
SC is the abbreviation for scene in a play script

explanation.surface: A head nun upstages everyone, taking the place of a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steals' just links: SC takes the place of one B. 'it matters' is a pun: an abscess produces matter, i.e. pus.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is a swelling filled with pus, which doctors call matter, so it 'matters'.

clue.text: Complaint each North American raised over train being held up

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upward, so in reverse
being held up in a down clue also turns the letters to read from bottom to top

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: Each American grumbles that a delayed train has been held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EA + NA into ANAE, and 'being held up' turns AIM into MIA; 'over' places the first above the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a medical condition, a shortage of red blood cells, and complaint means ailment.

clue.text: Contract hire's arranged, about five pounds

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the numeral
arranged says the letters of the fodder are set in a new order

parts.note: the word with its s supplies the five letters h i r e s
V is the Roman numeral for five
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A hire contract is drawn up, costing about five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives SHRIE, which 'about' splits round the numeral. 'Contract' is a verb, to shrink, not a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to wrinkle and shrink, i.e. to get smaller.

clue.text: I'll need to consult about

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'I'll need to consult about (7)', has no definition: the wordplay I inside CONFER gives the answer but the defining word (a tree) appears to be missing from the OCR text, and a search found no fuller version.

clue.text: Vain fellow seen in valley, about ninety

indicators.note: about says the valley word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a coomb is a short valley or hollow
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A conceited man is spotted in a dale, aged about ninety.
explanation.walkthrough: COOMB (also spelt combe) is a British word for a small valley; 'seen in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a conceited dandy, a show-off.

clue.text: Leading family makes payment to author

definitions.meaning: the reigning dynasty and its members
a fee paid to a writer on each copy sold

explanation.surface: The top household earns money from a writer's sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalty means both the monarch's kin and a percentage paid to a writer per book sold.

clue.text: Host's mad, losing head

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: The party host has gone crazy and lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' means a large crowd or armed force, not a party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a multitude, and in old usage specifically an army of soldiers.

clue.text: Replacement for medical photo lost internally

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: lost internally says the middle letters of the photo word go

parts.note: an X-ray is a medical photograph

explanation.surface: A substitute is needed for an X-ray that went missing inside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost internally' removes RA from the middle of XRAY, leaving XY.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a substitute authorised to act on another's behalf.

clue.text: Vehicle a short distance from the rear

indicators.note: from the rear says the word is read starting from its end

parts.note: a yard is a short distance, three feet

explanation.surface: A car is parked just a few steps behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low flat cart, the kind brewers used to deliver barrels.

clue.text: I'm penning note as part of list

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the note goes inside

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone writes down a musical note on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single entry in a list or inventory.

clue.text: Hide tin containing potassium and iodine

indicators.note: containing says the chemical symbol for tin holds the other two

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A can of chemicals is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun: an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal pelt, its outer covering.

clue.text: Ignition system found in old Russian sidecar?

definitions.text: Ignition system found in old Russian sidecar?

parts.words: Ignition system found in old Russian sidecar?
parts.note: a sidecar is a cocktail, and a firebomb named after an old Soviet foreign minister is a mixed drink that ignites

explanation.surface: A vintage Soviet motorbike sidecar hides its engine's starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sidecar' suggests a motorcycle attachment but is a brandy cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrol bomb named after Stalin's foreign minister, nicknamed after a mixed drink, is lit to set things ablaze.

clue.text: Infant, diminutive, left by outsiders -very bad

indicators.note: left by outsiders says the outer letters of the combined words are abandoned

parts.note: a baby is an infant
small means diminutive

explanation.surface: A tiny baby is abandoned by strangers, a terrible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: BABY SMALL loses its first and last letters, B and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly poor, dreadful.

clue.text: Cricket side in Derby terribly parched

indicators.note: in places the cricket side inside the rearranged letters
terribly signals the letters of the place name are badly jumbled

parts.note: on is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team in Derby is suffering in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes BEDRY, split by the side. In cricket the 'on side' is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone-dry means completely dry, utterly without moisture.
